content: Ritonavir increases the plasma levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, dexamethasone decreases the plasma levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, dexamethasone reduces the levels or effects of lopinavir through the same CYP3A4 metabolic pathway. Caution and close monitoring are advised when these drugs are co-administered. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dexfenfluramine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dextromethorphan by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. DHEA (herbal supplement) increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases the levels of diazepam by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases diazepam levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of buccal diazepam by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. However, it may also decrease buccal diazepam levels by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Ritonavir increases buccal diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the elimination rate of diazepam, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Close monitoring is necessary. Lopinavir decreases the levels or effects of intranasal diazepam by affecting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Ritonavir increases intranasal diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases intranasal diazepam levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lopinavir increases the effects of diazoxide through mechanisms not fully understood. Ritonavir also increases diazoxide effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. Lopinavir decreases the levels or effects of didanosine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir similarly decreases didanosine levels by increasing gastric pH. Both ritonavir and didanosine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir has a similar effect. Significant changes in plasma estrogen and progestin levels have been observed with HIV protease inhibitors. Monitoring for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache is recommended. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, reducing renal and hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Diltiazem increases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir and lopinavir also increase diltiazem levels through the same mechanism. Serious interactions necessitate the use of alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir has a similar effect. Serious interactions necessitate the use of alternative drugs. Disulfiram increases ritonavir toxicity by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. This interaction is contraindicated and applies only to the oral solution of ritonavir, which contains 42% alcohol. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir increases docetaxel levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. Lopinavir increases the levels of dofetilide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Ritonavir has a similar effect. Therapy modification or alternative drugs are recommended. Dofetilide increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Dolasetron and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of donepezil by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Donepezil and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Serious interactions necessitate the use of alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of doravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir has a similar effect. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase doravirine plasma concentrations and toxicities. Close monitoring is recommended. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of doxepin by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Doxepin and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Serious interactions necessitate the use of alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Lopinavir has a similar effect. Serious interactions necessitate the use of alternative drugs. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir has a similar effect. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Caution and monitoring are advised. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ritonavir and lopinavir also increase dronedarone levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction is contraindicated. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of duloxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dutasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Lopinavir has a similar effect. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib AUC, potentially increasing toxicity risks. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ritonavir has a similar effect. Dose adjustments may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for NVAF. Therapy modification or alternative drugs are recommended. Ritonavir and efavirenz both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz and lopinavir both prolong the QTc interval. Serious interactions necessitate the use of alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir has a similar effect. Serious interactions necessitate the use of alternative drugs. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of elagolix by mechanisms involving CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter but decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by mechanisms involving CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir has a similar effect. This interaction is contraindicated. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism.
